subject: ela
cluster: Range of reading and level of text complexity
intro: Informational texts come in many forms: science facts, biographies, how-to instructions, history passages, and more. Each type has features that help readers understand it. Good readers recognize what kind of text they are reading, find the main idea, identify supporting details, and notice how the author has organized the information.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Frogs are cold-blooded animals. This means their body temperature changes with the temperature of their surroundings. In winter, frogs hibernate underground or at the bottom of ponds. Their heartbeat slows down and they barely breathe until spring arrives.'

What is the main idea of this passage? Name one detail that supports it.

steps: I read through the passage to find what it is mainly about.
The passage talks about frogs being cold-blooded and what that means for their survival in winter.
The main idea is that frogs are cold-blooded animals and their body functions change with temperature.
One supporting detail is that frogs hibernate in winter and their heartbeat slows down.
solution.answer: The main idea is that frogs are cold-blooded animals whose body temperature and body functions are controlled by their surroundings. One supporting detail is that in winter frogs hibernate and their heartbeat slows down almost to a stop until spring.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Amelia Earhart was born in Kansas in 1897. She saw her first airplane at a fair when she was ten years old. As a young woman, she worked odd jobs to save money for flying lessons. In 1932, she became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean.'

This is a biography snippet. What is the main idea? List two details that help develop the story.

steps: A biography tells the story of a real person's life. This passage is about Amelia Earhart.
The main idea is that Earhart worked hard from an early age to become a record-breaking pilot.
Detail 1: She saw her first airplane at age ten and became interested in flying.
Detail 2: She worked odd jobs to save money for flying lessons.
These details show the steps that led to her crossing the Atlantic in 1932.
solution.answer: The main idea is that Amelia Earhart worked hard from a young age to pursue her passion for flying and became a record-breaking pilot. Two details: (1) She saw her first airplane at ten and became fascinated, and (2) she worked odd jobs to save money for flying lessons. Both details show the steps she took toward her historic solo flight.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'How to Make a Bird Feeder:
Step 1: Get a clean plastic bottle and punch small holes near the bottom.
Step 2: Push two sticks through the holes to make perches for birds to stand on.
Step 3: Fill the bottle with birdseed.
Step 4: Tie a string around the neck of the bottle and hang it from a tree branch.'

What kind of text is this? What is its purpose? Name the first step.

steps: This text has numbered steps, which tells me it is a how-to or procedural text.
Its purpose is to give instructions for making something.
The first step is to get a clean plastic bottle and punch small holes near the bottom.
solution.answer: This is a how-to (procedural) text. Its purpose is to give step-by-step instructions for making a bird feeder. The first step is to get a clean plastic bottle and punch small holes near the bottom.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'In 1903, Wilbur and Orville Wright built and flew the first powered airplane. The brothers ran a bicycle shop in Ohio. They used what they knew about balance and mechanics from building bikes to design wings that could be controlled. After years of testing gliders, they flew their powered plane at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, for 12 seconds.'

This passage is a history text. What is the main idea? Which detail best supports it?

steps: I read the passage. It is about the Wright brothers building and flying the first airplane.
The main idea is that the Wright brothers used knowledge from their bicycle work to invent powered flight.
The best supporting detail is that they used their understanding of balance and mechanics from building bikes to design controllable wings.
This detail directly explains how their prior experience made their invention possible.
solution.answer: The main idea is that the Wright brothers applied knowledge from their bicycle work to invent powered flight. The best supporting detail is that their experience with balance and mechanics from building bikes helped them design wings that could be controlled, which was the key to making a plane that could actually fly.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Earth has four layers. The outermost layer is the crust, which is the thin layer we live on. Below the crust is the mantle, made of hot, slowly moving rock. Deeper still is the outer core, made of liquid metal. At the very center is the inner core, a ball of solid metal.

What text structure does this passage use? What clue words helped you identify it?

steps: I read the passage. It describes four layers one at a time, starting from the outside and going deeper.
The passage moves in order from outermost to innermost, which is a sequential or spatial structure.
Clue words that help identify this: 'outermost,' 'below,' 'deeper still,' 'at the very center.'
These words show location and order, pointing to a spatial/sequence structure.
solution.answer: This passage uses a spatial or sequence text structure, describing each layer from outermost to innermost. Clue words like 'outermost,' 'below,' 'deeper still,' and 'at the very center' signal the order and direction, helping readers follow the structure from the surface of Earth to its core.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Spiders spin silk to make webs. The silk comes out of organs called spinnerets at the back of the spider's body. Spider silk is one of the strongest materials in nature for its weight. Webs are used to catch prey, protect eggs, and help spiders move from place to place.'

What is the main idea of this passage? Name two details that support it.
items.hint: The main idea is the most important point the passage is making. The details give specific information that backs up that point.

steps: The passage is mostly about spider silk and what spiders use it for.
Main idea: Spiders produce remarkable silk that serves many important purposes.
Detail 1: Silk comes from organs called spinnerets.
Detail 2: Webs are used to catch prey, protect eggs, and help spiders travel.
solution.answer: The main idea is that spiders produce strong silk from their spinnerets that serves multiple purposes. Two supporting details: (1) silk comes out of organs called spinnerets at the back of the spider, and (2) webs are used to catch prey, protect eggs, and help spiders move from place to place.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Benjamin Banneker was born free in Maryland in 1731. He was mostly self-taught and became an expert in astronomy and mathematics. In 1792, he sent a copy of his almanac to Thomas Jefferson along with a letter arguing that all people deserve equal rights. Jefferson wrote back and said he agreed.'

This is a biography. What is the main idea? What does the exchange with Jefferson show about Banneker?
items.hint: Ask yourself: what is the most important thing this passage wants you to know about Benjamin Banneker? What does his letter to Jefferson tell you about who he was?

steps: The passage tells us Banneker was self-taught, a scientist, and used his position to speak out for equal rights.
Main idea: Banneker was a remarkable self-taught scientist who also courageously advocated for equal rights.
The exchange with Jefferson shows that Banneker was not only an expert in science but also someone willing to challenge powerful leaders about justice.
solution.answer: The main idea is that Benjamin Banneker was a brilliant self-taught scientist and a courageous advocate for equal rights. The exchange with Jefferson shows that Banneker used his respected position as a scientist to speak directly to one of the most powerful people in America about equality, which shows he was both intellectually gifted and morally brave.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'How to Plant a Seed:
Step 1: Fill a small pot with potting soil.
Step 2: Poke a small hole in the soil with your finger.
Step 3: Drop one seed into the hole and cover it gently.
Step 4: Water the soil lightly so it is damp but not soaking wet.
Step 5: Place the pot near a sunny window and check it every day.'

What type of text is this? What would happen if you did Step 4 before Step 2?
items.hint: Think about what kind of text gives numbered steps. Then think about why the order of the steps matters in this text.

steps: This is a how-to or procedural text because it gives numbered instructions.
Step 2 tells you to poke a hole in the soil. Step 4 tells you to water after the seed is covered.
If you watered before poking the hole, the wet soil would be harder to work with and might not hold the hole open properly.
Order matters in how-to texts because each step depends on the previous one being done first.
solution.answer: This is a how-to (procedural) text. If you did Step 4 (watering) before Step 2 (poking the hole), the wet soil would be muddy and harder to poke a clean hole in. The order matters because you need the dry hole ready before adding the seed and then water.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Lightning strikes Earth about 100 times every second. A single bolt of lightning reaches temperatures of about 30,000 Kelvin, which is five times hotter than the surface of the sun. Lightning can travel from cloud to cloud or from a cloud to the ground. It follows the path of least resistance, which is why it often strikes tall objects like trees and towers.'

What is the main idea? What text structure does the author use? Name one clue word or phrase.
items.hint: Look at whether the passage is organized by sequence, cause-and-effect, compare-contrast, or just explaining facts about a topic. What connecting words do you see?

steps: The passage gives facts about lightning: how often it strikes, how hot it is, where it travels, and why it hits certain objects.
The main idea is that lightning is an incredibly powerful and frequent natural phenomenon.
The passage uses a cause-and-effect structure in the last sentence: lightning follows the path of least resistance, WHICH IS WHY it strikes tall objects.
Clue phrase: 'which is why' signals a cause-and-effect relationship.
solution.answer: The main idea is that lightning is an extremely powerful natural event that occurs constantly and behaves in predictable ways. The last sentence uses a cause-and-effect structure: lightning follows the path of least resistance, 'which is why' it strikes tall objects. The phrase 'which is why' is the clue that signals cause and effect.

items.prompt:
Read the passage below.

'Oceans and deserts seem like opposites. Oceans cover much of Earth and contain vast amounts of water. Deserts receive almost no rain and are among the driest places on Earth. Yet both are extreme environments where only specially adapted plants and animals can survive. Both also play important roles in Earth's climate system.'

What text structure does this passage use? Name two clue words. What is the main idea?
items.hint: Does the passage show how two things are the same or different, or both? Look for words that signal comparison or contrast.

steps: The passage talks about both oceans and deserts, comparing and contrasting them.
Text structure: compare-contrast.
Clue words: 'seem like opposites' (contrast) and 'yet both' (comparison).
The main idea is that although oceans and deserts seem like total opposites, they share important roles as extreme environments in Earth's climate.
solution.answer: The passage uses a compare-contrast structure. Clue words include 'seem like opposites' (signaling contrast) and 'yet both' (signaling comparison). The main idea is that despite being very different environments, oceans and deserts are both extreme habitats that play important roles in Earth's climate system.
